videos.title: How the OFF HAND affects Side Pressure in ARMWRESTLING
videos.summary:
How the off hand affects side pressure in armwrestling: what your non-pulling hand does can add serious kilos to your side pressure.

In this one I test it live on the crane scale. I pull side pressure in different positions, first with my off hand resting on top of the peg and then gripping and pulling into the table, to show how much the off hand really matters.

What I cover:
- How 1RMs do more than test your peak strength. They show you the biomechanical lane your body needs to be in to produce maximum force
- Why, once your elbow is conditioned to a certain level, how much body weight you can get into the movement decides the force your opponent feels, and why lightweights can't just lean
- Why resting your off hand on top of the peg is great for moving around and dropping below the table, but does nothing for side pressure
- How gripping the table, staying in contact with the peg and pulling down with your bicep and back has added 10 to 20 kilos to my side pressure, depending on the position
- Tests on the crane scale: 57 kg with my hand on top and shoulder back, 60.9 kg when hooking under the table, and 104.8 kg (a PR for that style) with my shoulder committed behind it at center table while pulling into the table
- Foot up vs foot down, and why repeated max efforts against an immovable object condition the elbow like crazy

What do you do with your off hand when you pull side pressure? Tell me in the comments.
